draft.title: DNA replication
card: DNA replication makes an exact copy of a cell's DNA before the cell divides. The enzyme helicase unzips the double helix by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the bases.
Each separated strand then acts as a template. The enzyme DNA polymerase adds free nucleotides to it, pairing A with T and C with G.
Each new DNA molecule has one old strand and one new strand. This is called semi-conservative replication.
Because bases pair in a fixed way, each copy has the same base sequence as the original. A mistake in pairing can change the sequence, which is one source of mutation.
draft.remember: Each strand is a template, so every new DNA molecule keeps one old strand and gains one new strand.

a.q: After one round of DNA replication, what does each new DNA molecule contain?
opts: One original strand and one new strand
Two new strands and no original DNA
A mix of short old and new pieces on each strand
a.why: Each original strand is used as a template for a new strand, so each molecule has one old and one new strand. Two original strands in one molecule would mean the old DNA was kept whole, but the old strands are separated and each ends up in a different molecule.
a.clue: Think about what each unzipped strand is used for.

b.q: A scientist grows bacteria for one round of replication so that all the new DNA is built from newly supplied nucleotides. Which result for the original strands fits the card?
opts: The two original strands end up in different DNA molecules
The two original strands stay paired in one DNA molecule
The original strands break down and are not reused
The original strands join to the new strands end to end
b.why: Helicase separates the original strands, and each one is a template for a new strand. So each original strand ends up paired with a new strand in a different molecule. The original strands staying together would be conservative copying, which does not happen.
b.clue: Each old strand is unzipped from its partner and then paired with something new.

a.best: One original strand and one new strand

b.best: The two original strands end up in different DNA molecules
